pages.title: No-Dig Steel Post Fencing
pages.text: ABETTERFOUNDATION No-Dig Steel Post Fencing Driven steel posts that hold tight in Toledo clay and stay put through freeze and thaw How it works Why it matters here We don’t dig holes or pour concrete. We drive 8-foot galvanized steel posts, 2⅜ inches across (Schedule 40 pipe), 4 feet into the ground and build the fence on them. No dirt piles and no torn-up lawn. Clay and freezing winters are hard on concrete footings. Water gets in, freezes, and pushes the post a little further out of line each year. A driven steel post has no footing to heave, and there’s no wood sitting in wet concrete to rot. Below frost line Posts driven deep, not floated in a footing Zero concrete Nothing underground to crack No cure time Panels go on as soon as the posts are in We check your soil at the estimate. Ask us to drive a test post. It takes about two minutes. CALL OR TEXT (419) 214-2107 THEGFSMETHOD

pages.title: Why We Drive Posts in Clay
pages.text: POSTINSTALLATION , COMPARED Why We Drive Posts in Clay The part you never see is the part that fails first. Three ways to set a post in Toledo clay. POOR Wood Post in Dirt The low-bid shortcut Post: PT wood 4x4 Set: Tamped dirt, ~2 ft deep ✓ Lowest price up front ✗ Whole buried post sits in wet soil ✗ Frost pushes it up each winter ✗ Leans as the dirt settles ✗ Usually the first post to fail BETTER Wood Post in Concrete The old neighborhood standard Post: PT wood 4x4 Set: Concrete, ~2.5 ft deep ✓ Holds straighter than dirt ✓ Familiar, widely used ✗ Rots where it meets the concrete ✗ Footing can heave in frost ✗ Hard to fix once it fails BEST ★RECOM M ENDE D Driven Steel Post Our King Plus method Post: 8 ft galv. Sch-40 steel, 2⅜" OD Set: Driven 4 ft, no concrete ✓ No concrete, so no frost heave ✓ Soil grips the full post ✓ Driven 4 ft, below the frost line ✓ Galvanized: won't rot or rust ✓ Bends on impact, won't crack POOR SOIL UPGRADE Steel Post in Concrete Driven posts need clay to grip. In sandy or loose soil we set PT wood posts in concrete. Want steel there instead? A galvanized steel post set about 3 ft deep in concrete is available as an upgrade. Driven a full 4 ft down. Toledo's frost line runs about 3 ft, so our posts anchor below it in undisturbed clay. The “+” in King Plus is an extra top rail that locks your pickets straight and crowns the fence. THEGFSMETHOD

pages.title: Why Cedar Holds Up Better Than Treated Pine
pages.text: CEDARVS . TREATEDPINE Why Cedar Holds Up Better Than Treated Pine It comes down to what's in the wood and how it handles our wet, freezing winters WOOD&CEDAR Thujaplicins Natural compounds in the heartwood that resist rot ~22 lb/ft³ Lightweight, easy on hardware No Chemicals Rot resistance is in the wood Stays Flatter Shrinks and twists less than PT as it dries Pressure-Treated: What to Expect Pressure-treated pine relies on chemical preservatives forced into the wood. The treatment doesn't reach all the way through, so cuts and cracks expose untreated wood. It also usually ships wet, so it shrinks, checks, and twists on your fence as it dries in place. Cedar is drier and moves less as it ages. Cedar Styles We Offer Board-on-Board Privacy No gaps, even after the boards dry Shadowbox Same look from both sides Lattice Top Privacy with a lattice band on top Premium Northern White Cedar. Sourced from Michigan's Upper Peninsula. The USDA Wood Handbook rates its heartwood “resistant to very resistant” to decay, its top rating.

pages.text: WOODPRIVACYSTYLESCOMPARED Standard vs Shadowbox vs Board-on-Board What each one looks like, and what you give up WOOD&CEDARGOOD Standard Privacy Dog Ear SPECIFICATIONS Privacy: 90–95% Look: Traditional Both sides: No — one finished face Airflow: Minimal Cost: $ PROS ✓ Most affordable option ✓ Classic neighborhood look ✓ Fastest to build ✓ Easy board replacement CONS ✗ Visible rails on back side ✗ Slight gaps between boards ✗ Less wind resistant ✗ One-sided appearance BETTER Shadowbox Alternating boards SPECIFICATIONS Privacy: 70–85% Look: Decorative Both sides: Yes — same on both Airflow: Good Cost: $$ PROS ✓ Attractive from both sides ✓ Good airflow & wind relief ✓ Your neighbor gets the same view ✓ Layered look, not a flat wall CONS ✗ Less privacy than solid ✗ Gaps visible at angles ✗ More material cost ✗ Takes a little longer to build BEST ★RECOM M ENDE D Board-on-Board Overlapping privacy SPECIFICATIONS Privacy: 100% Look: Solid, layered Both sides: Yes — finished both Airflow: Minimal Cost: $$$ PROS ✓ Complete privacy — no gaps ✓ The most solid-looking fence ✓ No see-through as boards dry ✓ Finished on both sides CONS ✗ Uses the most lumber ✗ Takes the longest to build ✗ Heavier fence ✗ Costs the most of the three Which one? pages.text: CEDARCARE Caring for Your Cedar Fence Cedar doesn’t need much. This is all of it. WOOD&CEDAR Sealing OPTIONAL , YEAR 1 Seal it to hold the color, or leave it bare and let it turn silver-gray. Either is fine. It only changes the look. Stain / Re-seal EVERY 3 – 5 YEARS If you sealed it, reapply every three to five years depending on how much direct sun that run of fence takes. Inspect & Clean ANNUAL Walk the line once a year: check for loose boards, clear leaves and debris, and trim back vegetation growing into the fence. Want a price on cedar? Free estimate. pages.title: Frequently Asked Questions
pages.text: COMMONQUESTIONS Frequently Asked Questions Straight answers up front — and a real person at (419) 214-2107 for the rest WORKINGWITHUSQ. How long does installation take? Most residential fences go up in 1–3 days, and we install all winter — we can drive posts into frozen ground. The crew cleans up daily. Q. Do I need a permit? Most local zoning requires one. We pull and handle permits for you — it's built into every quote. Q. Do you offer financing? Yes — financing is available for qualifying customers. Ask us for current terms and rates. Q. What's the warranty? Three years on workmanship from us, plus the manufacturers’ limited lifetime warranties on Homeland vinyl and Elite aluminum. Q. Do I need to be home during the install? No — but we recommend being there for the first and final walkthroughs so you and the crew stay on the same page. Q. What areas do you serve? Northwest Ohio & Southeast Michigan — Toledo, Perrysburg, Maumee, Sylvania, Monroe, Temperance, and nearby. More questions? Call or text (419) 214-2107 · ghareebfence.com — we're happy to help.

pages.title: What's Actually in Your Quote
pages.text: COMPAREAPPLESTOAPPLES What's Actually in Your Quote The lowest number isn't always the lowest price. Here's what we spell out — and what's easy to leave off a cheaper bid. IN E V ERY G FS Q U OT E ✓ Post type, size, and depth (in writing) ✓ Cedar species and grade, in writing ✓ Steel or aluminum gate frames and hardware ✓ Post foundation matched to your soil ✓ Full grading and cleanup, debris hauled ✓ Permits pulled and handled ✓ 3-year written workmanship warranty ✓ One accountable crew, owner on site E A SY TO L EAV EOFFABID ✗ “Posts in concrete” with no depth listed ✗ Lumber just called “cedar” — which grade? ✗ Gate hardware added on later ✗ One method for every yard, clay or sand ✗ Grading and cleanup billed separately ✗ “Permit is your responsibility” ✗ A verbal warranty only ✗ Subcontractors, no single point of contact Missing any of these? Then it isn’t cheaper. It just covers less. Ask for each one in writing before you compare prices. WORKINGWITHUS
